summary: Weekly POC sync to review pilot economics. Team reviewed recent benchmark numbers, caching impact, and batching tradeoffs. transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, audio ok?
[00:08] Marta: Yep, good here.
[00:12] Jordan: Cool. This is our weekly CloudBurst pilot econ sync. Agenda — go over the numbers from last run, talk caching and batching, and finalize next steps. Priya, do you want to start with the updated benchmark?
[00:28] Priya: Yeah, sure. So last Friday we ran 10k requests across the hosted test cluster and the dedicated staging pool. There were two main configs: baseline (no KV/prefix cache) and cache-enabled with a 40% effective hit rate on prefixes for the chat workload. The important numbers: baseline tokens/sec per dollar was about 1,250 tokens/$ on the hosted small instance profile; with caching that improved to ~2,150 tokens/$. I want to caution that's dependent on hit-rate; at 20% hit the uplift is only to ~1,600 tokens/$.
[01:10] Ben: Wait, when you say tokens per dollar is that amortized over GPU hours or per-request billing?
[01:16] Priya: It's GPU-hour normalized for the dedicated numbers — we computed total tokens generated in the run divided by GPU-hour cost for the time window. For hosted we used the API per-token equivalent unit cost from the spreadsheet Jordan sent earlier.
[01:28] Jordan: Right, and just to be clear the dedicated numbers assume our current reserved capacity SKU with the pilot discount. If you switch to full Reserved you'd see slightly lower unit costs, but you'd be committing.
[01:40] Sara: How did batching affect latency? Our product owner is worried about p95 tail for chat.
[01:46] Priya: Good question. We tested batch sizes of 1, 4, and 8. For batch=1 p50 is ~120ms, p95 ~320ms on the dedicated 80GB GPU; batch=4 p50 increases to ~160ms, p95 to ~420ms. Batch=8 pushes p50 to 230ms and p95 to ~700ms. So there's a clear tradeoff: batching improves tokens/sec/$ by roughly 1.8x at batch=4 and 2.6x at batch=8, but tail latency becomes questionable for chat. For rerank/embedding routes batch=8 is probably fine.
[02:28] Marta: Those numbers are helpful. Our main product path is interactive chat, but we do some batch reranking during off-peak. Ideally we want to keep p95 under 400ms for chat.
[02:38] Priya: If your SLO is p95 < 400ms I'd recommend using adaptive batching: default batch size 1 for chat with opportunistic batching up to 4 during idle microbursts, and batch 8 for rerank flows. That preserves low tail latencies and gives the cost benefits where acceptable.
[02:54] Ben: Does Redwood support that adaptive batching out of the box?
[02:58] Priya: Yes — the runtime has request-level routing hints and service-level policies. We can configure per-route batching profiles and also set a latency cap so the scheduler will flush early if the time cap is hit.
[03:10] Alex: Curious about the KV cache — is that prefix only or full KV cache? How does it work with our prompt templates?
[03:16] Priya: It's a prefix/response cache optimized for repeated prompts and system text. For your template-heavy support replies we saw high reuse on the system/preamble tokens. The cache stores token-level KV state for compatible model families; you need to ensure prompt normalization to maximize hits. We saw normalization lift hit‑rate by about 5–7 percentage points when we canonicalized timestamps and ticket IDs.
[03:40] Sara: Any concerns about cache consistency or data residency? We need audit logs for compliance.
[03:45] Jordan: Yes — for Dedicated/Private deployments, cache resides in your VPC and is subject to your KMS controls. Audit logs and cache metrics are exportable to your SIEM. We'll attach SOC2 notes.
[03:56] Marta: Good. About the economics spreadsheet — Jordan you updated it with tokens/sec/$ but we want a route-level breakdown (chat vs rerank vs embeddings).
[04:05] Jordan: Yep, I added per-route tabs. Right now rough numbers: chat baseline 1,250 tokens/$; chat with adaptive batching + 40% cache hit 2,000 tokens/$; rerank baseline 4,200 tokens/$ with batch=8 and no cache; embeddings ~6,800 tokens/$ on quantized model. I'll send the sheet after this call.
[04:26] Ben: Quick Q: embeddings numbers used quantized int8, right? Any observed quality delta?
[04:32] Priya: We used the recommended quantization profile for the model; embeddings delta was negligible for your search workload (cosine similarity drop < 0.3%). But we flagged a small regression on abstractive summarization tests — that route we should keep unquantized for quality.
[04:50] Marta: On the procurement side, procurement wants to know the expected burn rate for a 3-month pilot if we run chat at current traffic (~12k qps? actually, not qps, sorry — 12k messages/day).
[05:02] Jordan: No worries. Using chat per-message token average of 230 tokens, 12k messages/day -> 2.76M tokens/day. At 2,000 tokens/$ that maps to about $1,380/day or ~$41k/month. That's under the pilot reserved SKU estimate. If you remove caching or hit-rate drops to 20% that goes up to ~ $62k/month.
[05:28] Sara: Those are big swings. We need to quantify sensitivity — maybe show a heatmap of cost vs cache hit-rate and batch mix.
[05:34] Priya: We can run sensitivity sims. I'll add an axis for hit-rate, batch distribution (percent chat batched at 1/4/8), and model quantization levels.
[05:44] Ben: For the larger benchmark run — what's the OOM / memory profile? We had one run where the KV cache caused memory spikes on the 80GB GPU.
[05:52] Priya: Right — that was due to unbounded per-request KV entries with a high repetition of long contexts. Fixes: 1) enable KV eviction policy (LRU) and cap total KV entries per session; 2) use truncated context window for history; 3) if needed use split-sharding so KV lives in host memory and fetches lazily. With the eviction cap we saw memory stabilize. We'll include the config we used in the benchmark artifact.
[06:18] Marta: Great. On next steps, we want the bigger cached vs uncached run to be representative of our prod traffic distribution. Ben will upload the prompt sets.
[06:26] Ben: I'll drop those in the shared drive by Friday.
[06:29] Jordan: Awesome. Anything else — competitors were mentioned in procurement as alternatives. Marta, did they ask for a comparison?
[06:36] Marta: They wanted a short note comparing to OpenAI hosted pricing and an operational note about on-prem.
[06:41] Jordan: We'll include a one-page competitor cost + ops pros/cons in the follow-up.
[06:47] Alex: One more: can we get a quick demo of the canary rollback for dedicated routing? Our infra lead wants to see failover behavior.
[06:54] Priya: Yes — Priya here, I can set up a 15–20 minute demo. We'll show canary deploy to 10% traffic then trigger simulated capacity loss and show automatic fallback to hosted variant.
[07:07] Jordan: Let's schedule that for week of 2025-11-17. I'll send a calendar invite.
[07:12] Marta: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:15] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[07:18] [end of recording]
